summary: Hisayoshi Miyamoto is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under traditional teacher Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi. Attested in 2026, he holds lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, where he is attested as a lecturer from 1986 to 1992 and as a professor in 2015.

Hitoshi Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar. In 1992, he was a part-time lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and Nara University of Education, and a research assistant at Otani University; he was affiliated with Osaka University in 2016.

Hjalmar Frisk (1900–1984) was a Swedish linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Gothenburg. He taught at Lund University in 1937 and served as Professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics and Sanskrit at Gothenburg from 1938 to 1967.

Hla Pe (1913–2007) was a linguist who earned his MA from the University of Rangoon and a doctorate from SOAS University of London. He taught Burmese language and culture at SOAS from 1948 and served as Professor of Burmese from 1966 to 1980.
Ho-chin Yang specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Washington in 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.
Hogen Bays works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Shodo Harada and serves as co-abbot at Great Vow Zen Monastery.
Hoin Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Gyōin Hashimoto around 1953 and received his education at Ryukoku University.
Hoju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University from circa 1998 to 2002 and at KU Leuven from circa 2005 to 2007. Hoju also taught Kyokuga Saeki.

Hoju Shioda works in Buddhist studies. Attested in 2026, Shioda has held posts including assistant director at Minobusan University and lecturer roles associated with Minobusan University, Doho University, and Daido University Graduate School.

Hojun Nagasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He was a professor at Otani University from circa 1974 to 1999 and became president of the Japan Association of Jain Studies in 1998.
Hokai (1768–1834) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hogetsu and Zuihe.
Hokei Izumi (1884–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani University under Bunyiu Nanjio and served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1925 to 1947.
Hoko Kuwana is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (attested 2015) and holds a director post at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Holden Furber (1903–1993) was a historian and Indologist educated at Oxford and Harvard. He taught history at Harvard and the University of Texas at Austin before serving as Professor of South Asia Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (1948–1973).

Holger Pedersen (1867–1953) was a Danish linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen and studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Greifswald. He served as a lecturer and professor at the University of Copenhagen from 1897.

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University from circa 2002 to 2009 and took up a post at the University of Colorado Boulder around 2008.

Holmes Welch (1924–1981) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned his BA and MA at Harvard University. He later served as a lecturer at Harvard (circa 1963–1976) and at Yale University.

Hong Luo is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who received a PhD from Peking University (2007). He worked at China Tibetology Research Center (2007–2017), became professor at Sichuan University in 2018, and is a Research Fellow at Hamburg.
Hongyue Guo works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Guo studied under Xubang Qi and completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2007) under the supervision of Stephen R. Bokenkamp.
